subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Swedish Coffee Experiment
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Swedish Coffee Experiment usable.

hook.text: In the 1750s, Sweden's King Gustav III tried to prove coffee was poison—using an experiment on condemned prisoners.

buildup.text: Two identical twins were sentenced to death. One was ordered to drink three pots of coffee daily, the other three pots of tea.

discovery.text: The experiment was monitored by physicians for years. Both prisoners survived long beyond expectations—outliving their doctors.

twist.text: The tea drinker died first—at age 83. The coffee drinker lived even longer. Coffee was vindicated, and the ban was dropped.

climax.text: King Gustav III was assassinated in 1792—long before the experiment concluded. He never saw coffee's acquittal.

punchline.text: The king died. The doctors died. The coffee drinker lived longest. Case closed.

quiz.question: What happened in the Swedish coffee experiment with twin prisoners?
options: Both lived past 80—the tea drinker died first, vindicating coffee
